title.narrative: Creating an enabling environment for NGO humanitarian Operations in Somalia/Somaliland through the Somali NGO Consortium's coordination and information sharing.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSomalia continues to face challenges in governance despite gradual progress in political and democratic spaces. Consequently, government institutions (both at FMS and FGS ) remain with visible capacity gaps and resource constraints to objectively and effectively provide essential services and humanitarian leadership in coordination, oversight, and support within the IASC aid architecture and humanitarian principles. In addressing this gap, national and international NGOs have thus grown in number (to 321 and 61, respectively) with a reported presence in 18 regions and 73 districts (2024 HNRP). A well-coordinated and inclusive humanitarian system thus remains paramount in balancing technical requirements, operational constraints, evolving contextual realities, power dynamics and individual interests of key stakeholders (i.e. affected communities, state actors, UN agencies, NGOs and institutional donors).ltbrgtAcknowledging the fact that “Somalia ranks second globally for its exposure to natural hazards and only fourth in terms of its ability to address and cope with these recurrent catastrophes”, concerted and coordinated NGOs’ efforts in providing humanitarian assistance remain key. With the humanitarian space characterized by several bottlenecks including (but not limited to) weak government institutions, funding constraints and accessibility constraints, effective and inclusive coordination remains critical for NGOs (who have been providing critical life-saving humanitarian assistance).ltbrgtThrough this project, the SNC seeks to contribute towards “conducive and inclusive humanitarian spaces where International and national (including women-led and Minority Rights Organizations-MROs) NGOs have access to the necessary information, resources, and operations at FGS and FMS levels”. Improved and inclusive coordination and information sharing (at national and area-based levels will facilitate effective information exchange, replication or scaling up of best practices and addressing operational/pragmatic impediments collectively. This will contribute immensely towards improving the country humanitarian system putting into consideration all input and positions from all stakeholders, i.e. government stakeholders, UN agencies, donors, INGOs and national NGOs (including women-led and MROs). ltbrgtLastly, the project seeks to support processes, and activities aimed at removing or reducing the negative impact of Bureaucratic administrative impediments (BAIs) that would stifle, or distort the delivery of life-saving interventions. BAIs like denial of tax clearance, withdrawal of registration to humanitarian agencies, and government directives on critical humanitarian sectors including WASH, Cash programs, Access, etc. all require a strong coordinative effort, lobbying, and deliberation which processes this project will facilitate.ltbrgtlt/pgt
